To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

students' use of technology for language learning can be described as self initiated learning, which is supported by mobile devices and the Internet, and that students' learning practices are characterized by the need for flexibility, autonomy and individuality.

(i) design needs to take into account the pervasive nature of the mobile technology use in students' daily lives, and that (ii) students prefer to learn on their own, and thus the design should provide tools for individual learning.

(i) mobile technologies should be integrated into distance learning environments in order to support students' individual learning, (ii) the integration of mobile technologies into distance learning environments should be based on the students' use practices, and not on the teachers' perceptions, and (iii), mobile learning should be designed to support students' self initiated learning tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to integrate mobile technology into distance higher education and the challenges of designing mobile learning applications for distance language learning.
understanding how students use technology in their daily lives and what this implies for designing mobile applications in distance education.
how students use technology in their learning, and what implications these findings have for the design of mobile applications for second-language learning in online/distant education.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
students use their own mobile technologies for language learning in their private time, and that the course design and materials should be adapted to this practice.
students' mobile technologies should be integrated into distance education courses, and that course designers need to consider how to design for students' habitual use practices.
the integration of mobile technology should be based on students' habitual and preferred use of technology in their learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design of mobile applications for language learning needs to take into account students' learning practices and their use of technology.
students' mobile technology practices are important in the design of mobile applications for second/foreign language learning in distance education.
students need to have access to a range of software tools on mobile devices that are easy to use, and that are integrated into their habitual use practices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of mobile applications for language learning should take into consideration the students' use of their mobile technologies in practice.
mobile technology is an important aspect of students' learning practice and should be considered in the design of mobile applications for language learning.
course designers should consider students' learning practices when designing mobile learning applications for distance education.
